title: Introduce compatibility crosswalk and concise release summarizer
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: onboarding churn and noisy release notes have made it hard for SREs and product owners to triage model-version rollouts. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a compatibility crosswalk that canonicalizes legacy and vendor-specific model metadata into the registry canonical schema, and a concise release summarizer that auto-generates a short human-friendly blurb for changelogs based on profile diffs. The crosswalk maps legacy fields (e.g., model.family, model.variant_tag, gpu_tier labels) and normalizes quantization/precision metadata into the registry's canonical keys so downstream tools (release assembler, perf dashboards) can reason about variants consistently. The summarizer consumes the profile delta output (performance, latency P50/P95, token cost, embedding/accuracy deltas) and applies heuristics: significance thresholds, affinity-aware weighting (prefers customer-affinity metrics when available), and a suppression filter to avoid trivial churn (e.g., insignificant lint-only metadata changes). It produces a 1-3 line synopsis plus a structured context note for machine-readable release bundles. Checklist: - [x] compatibility crosswalk implementation (python module) - [x] summarizer core logic and unit tests - [x] integration tests with onboard pipeline and release-assembler -> sample artifacts - [x] CI coverage for canonicalization edge cases (missing fields, vendor aliases) - [x] add provenance stamps (profile-hash + crosswalk-version) - [x] docs: crosswalk mapping table and summarized release note examples Implementation notes: - crosswalk lives at src/crosswalk/canonicalizer.py and includes a small, extensible alias table and tests for alias resolution. - summarizer implemented as a lightweight Rust binary (tools/release_summarizer) to match existing release tooling; it accepts profile-diff JSON and outputs both concise text and a compact JSON context blob. - integrated a new step in pipelines/onboard-release to call the summarizer and attach synthesized_blurb to release metadata. - added a release pipeline flag release.notes.auto_review to toggle human review requirement when the delta is above certain signal thresholds. Testing: unit tests added under tests/crosswalk and tests/summarizer; a staged integration run was executed against a synthetic delta (see sample-artifacts/example-delta.json) with expected blurb produced. Backwards compatibility: crosswalk includes schema versioning and a compatibility-mode that preserves original fields under vendor_provenance when requested. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind registry feature-flag registry.features.crosswalk_v1; will enable for 10% of onboard flows for 48h, evaluate noise metrics, then ramp. Related: links to ENG-4129 (onboard metadata stability) and SUP-7642 (customer report: noisy changelogs). Notes: This PR intentionally avoids enforcing a rigid semantic version bump on existing profiles; instead it emits recommended semantic hints for maintainers.
